missionPremise: P-296 (cortex-api, serving revision cortex-api-00472-web @ image 7219b707) computes and serves a real ETJ determination on the customer-facing cortex route (point-in-polygon against tx_etj_boundary, 355 rings). The Property Explorer BFF GET /api/spine/property-atoms/:id/facets discards it and serves the literal string 'unresolved', because (a) a type guard rejects any cortex cityLimitsFact whose etjStatus is not that literal, and (b) the record-path composer hardcodes the literal in all of its branches. designDecision.oneWriter: A single new module, apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/pe-etj-determination.ts, owns the transition from (cityLimits status, raw ETJ determination in hand) to the served four-state etjStatus + carried etjFact + declared etjConflict. Both adoption points call it: (a) atom-chain-to-facets.ts withCityLimitsFact (cortex-root adoption) and (b) pe-record-to-facets.ts composeCityLimits / recordUnavailableCityLimits (record composition and outage). No second implementation of the rule exists, so there is nothing for a divergence test to police (DEV_PROCESS 2.4).
designDecision.fourStates: etjStatus is widened from the single literal 'unresolved' to the union "present" | "absent" | "unresolved" | "conflicting".
designDecision.idempotency: The resolver's raw input is cityLimitsFact.etjFact.status when a valid etjFact block is present, else the top-level etjStatus; a served 'conflicting' maps back to raw 'present'. This makes normalisation idempotent across the two adoption points (the cortex-root fact is normalised first, then the record composer re-reads it as its prior) without adding a second field, and it is lossless because 'conflicting' is produced only by incorporated + raw present.
designDecision.conflictRule: conflicting is emitted ONLY for (cityLimitsStatus == incorporated AND raw etj == present). incorporated+absent and unincorporated+present are coherent and serve absent / present respectively. That is exactly the dispatch's rule; anything broader would invent a conflict the dispatch did not ask for.
designDecision.neverDerive: If neither etjFact.status nor a present/absent top-level etjStatus is in hand, the state is unresolved and basis gains an explicit reason. ETJ is never derived from city limits and city limits is never derived from ETJ.
designDecision.cardDisplay: fact-sheet-resolver.ts's etjSuffix gains present / conflicting branches and loses its `?? "unresolved"` default, so the row a customer reads reflects the served state instead of a fallback literal.

mechanismQuestions.stated: The dispatch requires a SECOND mechanism to be stated before settling on one for the incorporated+present co-occurrence, and says 'Measure; do not pick.'
candidates: M1 — the city-limits read is the wrong one: landing_parcel_jurisdiction reports the jurisdiction that governs the point (the city, whose ETJ it is), not whether the point is inside city limits; an ETJ parcel would then read 'incorporated' falsely.
M2 — the ETJ ring is drawn to the city's outer boundary or is a limited-purpose annexation the city treats as not-in-ETJ.
M3 — the ETJ ring is stale relative to the current city limits.
M4 — the city-limits read is stale relative to a recent annexation.
M5 — both reads are correct and the parcel is genuinely both in city limits and in a published ETJ ring (a data defect on the ETJ publisher side).
mechanismQuestions.howMeasured: M1/M4 are distinguishable from M2/M3/M5 only against the stores (tx_city_boundary / tx_etj_boundary / landing_parcel_jurisdiction). This lane's reachable credential set is being checked at CP2; the dispatch's item 4 (co-occurrence count) is the decisive read and is reported either way. If no store credential is reachable from this seat, the close says so explicitly rather than substituting a guess (P-204's own close has the precedent: its close names the same credential gap).
